# Platform hardening

> Security baselines and hardening guidance for Windows, Linux, macOS, and mobile devices.

Part of the [domain list](README.md). 44 resources in 5 sections. Managing fleets of devices sits in Endpoint and device management; framework-level control catalogs sit in GRC and security program.

For references, how-to guides, and learning paths on this subject, see the TeamStarWolf library's [matching domain page](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/hubs/platform-hardening.md).

## Baselines and benchmarks

Which published baseline should this system meet?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Device security guidance](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/device-security-guidance) | NCSC, a part of GCHQ | NCSC collection for organizations securing phones, tablets, laptops, and desktops, with guides for general readers and for IT administrators, pages by platform, and case studies. | Reference | Free |
| [NIST SP 800-190](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/190/final) | NIST | Explains container technology, risks to images, registries, orchestrators, containers, and host operating systems, countermeasures for those risks, threat scenarios, and security across the life cycle. | Standard | Free |
| [NIST SP 800-124 Rev. 2](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/124/r2/final) | NIST | Covers threats to enterprise mobile devices and their management systems, device-side and enterprise security technologies, mitigations, and a deployment life cycle from requirements to disposal. | Standard | Free |
| [Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs)](https://www.cyber.mil/stigs/) | Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) | Home of the DoD's Security Requirements Guides and STIGs, with a document library that includes SCAP benchmarks, automation content, Group Policy Objects, and library compilations. | Standard | Free |
| [National Checklist Program Checklist Repository](https://ncp.nist.gov/repository) | NIST | Searchable repository of security configuration checklists, filtered by type, issuing authority, target product, content type, and tool compatibility, with download links. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [CIS Benchmarks](https://www.cisecurity.org/cis-benchmarks) | Center for Internet Security | Consensus configuration recommendations for many vendor product families, used as hardening baselines. | Standard | Free with account |

Listed here from another domain: CIS Benchmarks ([GRC and security program](grc-and-security-program.md#frameworks-controls-and-benchmarks)).

## Windows hardening

How do I harden Windows clients and servers?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Security baselines guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/device-management/windows-security-configuration-framework/windows-security-baselines) | Microsoft | Microsoft's guide to Windows security baselines, including what a baseline is, principles behind the settings, and where to get them, by download or through Intune. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit - How to use](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/device-management/windows-security-configuration-framework/security-compliance-toolkit-10) | Microsoft | Microsoft's page on the Security Compliance Toolkit, with sections on its tools: Policy Analyzer, LGPO, Set Object Security, and GPO to Policy Rules. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Windows Security documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's hub for Windows security documentation, with entry points for hardware security, operating system security, identity protection, application security, cloud services, security foundation, and privacy. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Attack surface reduction (ASR) rules reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference) | Microsoft | Reference to Defender's attack surface reduction rules: operating system and deployment method support, alerts and notifications, then details of standard protection rules and the others. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Application Control for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/) | Microsoft | Entry point to Microsoft's App Control for Business and AppLocker documentation, including policy design, policy configuration, deployment, and troubleshooting of App Control events. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Microsoft recommended driver block rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/design/microsoft-recommended-driver-block-rules) | Microsoft | Microsoft's vulnerable driver blocklist: when Windows enforces it, blocking the listed drivers with App Control, download and apply steps, and the blocklist as XML. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [BitLocker device encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/bitlocker/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's overview of BitLocker, including BitLocker To Go, its use of the TPM, system and licensing requirements, and how device encryption differs. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Credential Guard](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/credential-guard/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's overview of Credential Guard, which isolates credentials with virtualization-based security: where it is on by default, and hardware, licensing, and application requirements. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Protect devices from exploits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/exploit-protection) | Microsoft | Microsoft's page on Windows exploit protection: supported versions, its events in the Defender portal, advanced hunting, and Event Viewer, and a comparison of mitigations. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [System audit policy recommendations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/plan/security-best-practices/audit-policy-recommendations) | Microsoft | Microsoft's audit policy recommendations for Windows workstations and servers, including recommended settings by operating system, events to monitor, and what to watch in Active Directory. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [HardeningKitty](https://github.com/scipag/HardeningKitty) | scip AG | PowerShell tool that checks a Windows configuration against finding lists and can harden it, with modes including Audit, Config, Backup, and HailMary. | Tool | Free |
| [Harden Windows Security](https://github.com/HotCakeX/Harden-Windows-Security) | Violet Hansen (HotCakeX) | Home of the Harden System Security and AppControl Manager apps for Windows, which apply hardening through Microsoft's supported methods and manage App Control policies. | Tool | Free |
| [Windows LAPS overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/laps/laps-overview) | Microsoft | Introduces Windows LAPS for managing local administrator passwords: supported platforms, use with Microsoft Entra ID, policy settings, and migration from legacy Microsoft LAPS. | Vendor documentation | Free |

## Linux and container hardening

How do I harden a Linux host and the containers on it?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Ubuntu Security Guide (USG)](https://documentation.ubuntu.com/security/compliance/usg/) | Canonical | Canonical's documentation for USG, which audits and hardens Ubuntu against CIS Benchmark and DISA STIG profiles; it installs through the Ubuntu Pro client. | Vendor documentation | Freemium |
| [SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP7 Security and Hardening Guide](https://documentation.suse.com/sles/15-SP7/html/SLES-all/book-security.html) | SUSE | SUSE's guide for SLES 15 SP7, in parts including authentication, local security, network security, regulations and compliance, and confining privileges with AppArmor. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Security - ArchWiki](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Security) | Arch Linux | ArchWiki's recommendations for hardening Arch Linux, in sections including passwords, storage, user setup, mandatory access control, kernel hardening, sandboxing applications, and network and firewalls. | Reference | Free |
| [Kernel Self-Protection Project: Recommended Settings](https://kspp.github.io/Recommended_Settings) | Kernel Self-Protection Project | The Kernel Self-Protection Project's list of hardening settings for a Linux kernel: build CONFIG options by architecture, kernel command line options, and sysctls. | Reference | Free |
| [kernel-hardening-checker](https://github.com/a13xp0p0v/kernel-hardening-checker) (formerly kconfig-hardened-check) | Alexander Popov (a13xp0p0v) | Tool that checks a Linux kernel's Kconfig options, command line arguments, and sysctl parameters against hardening recommendations; it can also generate a Kconfig fragment. | Tool | Free |
| [The SELinux Notebook](https://github.com/SELinuxProject/selinux-notebook) | SELinux Project | Book about SELinux, open source and kept as Markdown in a repository: read it on GitHub, or build EPUB, PDF, or HTML copies from source. | Reference | Free |
| [AppArmor Documentation](https://apparmor.net/) | AppArmor | AppArmor's official documentation: getting started, writing and managing profiles, troubleshooting and monitoring, and background pages including a comparison with SELinux, with notes on recent releases. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [OpenSSH guidelines](https://infosec.mozilla.org/guidelines/openssh) | Mozilla | Mozilla's configuration guidelines for OpenSSH servers and clients, including modern and intermediate settings, multi-factor authentication, cipher and algorithm choices, key generation, and key protection. | Reference | Free |
| [SSH Hardening Guides](https://www.ssh-audit.com/hardening_guides.html) | Positron Security | Step-by-step SSH hardening commands for named operating system releases, in server, client, community-developed, and legacy groups, from the makers of ssh-audit. | Reference | Free |
| [Fail2Ban](https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban) | Fail2Ban | Log-watching daemon that blocks addresses with too many failed logins; the repository gives installation and configuration steps, contact channels, and the license. | Tool | Free |
| [AIDE - Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment](https://aide.github.io/) | AIDE | Host integrity checker that records file attributes and message digests in a database and reports later changes; the site lists features, packages, and help channels. | Tool | Free |
| [USBGuard](https://usbguard.github.io/) | USBGuard | Allows or blocks USB devices on Linux by rule, through kernel device authorization: a daemon, rule language, command-line and GUI interfaces, and C++ API. | Tool | Free |
| [Docker Engine security](https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/) | Docker Inc | Docker's review of Engine security: kernel namespaces, control groups, the daemon's attack surface, Linux capabilities, content trust signature verification, and other kernel security features. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Docker Bench for Security](https://github.com/docker/docker-bench-security) | Docker | Script that tests a Docker host and its containers against the CIS Docker Benchmark; runs from the host or as a container. | Tool | Free |
| [Kubernetes Security Checklist](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/security-checklist/) | Kubernetes | Kubernetes' baseline security checklist, covering network security, authentication and authorization, secrets, images, pod security and placement, admission controllers, and logs and auditing. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [kube-bench](https://github.com/aquasecurity/kube-bench) | Aqua Security | Checks a Kubernetes cluster against the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark, with tests defined in YAML and job files for EKS, AKS, GKE, and other managed services. | Tool | Free |

Listed here from another domain: kube-bench ([Cloud and infrastructure](cloud-and-infrastructure.md#audit-posture-and-runtime-tools)).

## macOS and mobile hardening

How do I harden Macs, iPhones, and Android devices?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [macOS Security Compliance Project](https://pages.nist.gov/macos_security/) | NIST | Home of mSCP, open source security guidance for Apple operating systems: how-to guides for generating configuration profiles, compliance scripts, baselines, and guidance documents. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [Apple Platform Security](https://support.apple.com/guide/security/welcome/web) | Apple | Apple's guide to the security of its devices, with chapters including hardware security, app security, system security, services security, and encryption and Data Protection. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [macOS Security and Privacy Guide](https://github.com/drduh/macOS-Security-and-Privacy-Guide) | drduh | Community guide to hardening Apple silicon Macs running macOS, in sections including threat model, FileVault, Lockdown Mode, firewall, DNS, browsers, and malware. | Reference | Free |
| [Objective-See's Tools](https://objective-see.org/tools.html) | Objective-See Foundation | Free, open source macOS security tools, including the LuLu firewall, BlockBlock and KnockKnock for persistence, ReiKey for keyboard event taps, and Netiquette for network connections. | Tool | Free |
| [About Lockdown Mode](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105120) | Apple | Apple's article on Lockdown Mode, including who it is for, what it restricts, enabling it on iPhone, iPad, or Mac, and excluding apps or websites. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Android security features](https://source.android.com/docs/security/features) | Google (Android Open Source Project) | Android Open Source Project summary of platform security features, including Verified Boot, the Trusty TEE, SELinux, Keystore, encryption, biometrics, authentication, app signing, and application sandbox. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [GrapheneOS features overview](https://grapheneos.org/features) | GrapheneOS | GrapheneOS's feature list for its hardened Android-based phone OS, including exploit mitigations, sandboxed Google Play, network and sensor permission toggles, and Storage Scopes. | Vendor documentation | Free |

## Audit and assessment tools

How do I measure a host against a baseline?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Lynis](https://cisofy.com/lynis/) | CISOfy | Tool that audits a Linux, macOS, or Unix host and suggests hardening steps, with sections including tests, plugins, and supported standards; Lynis Enterprise is paid. | Tool | Freemium |
| [ComplianceAsCode content](https://github.com/ComplianceAsCode/content) | ComplianceAsCode | Builds security policy content as SCAP, Ansible, and Bash; README sections include scan targets, installing from packages, release ZIPs, or source, and scanning with oscap. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [DevSec Hardening Framework](https://dev-sec.io/) | DevSec Hardening Framework Team | Open source hardening baselines for servers and services, including Linux, SSH, Docker, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Apache, and Nginx, published for Ansible, Chef, and Puppet. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [Goss](https://github.com/goss-org/goss) | goss-org | YAML-based validator for a server's configuration that can generate tests from current system state and serve results as a health endpoint, with dgoss for containers. | Tool | Free |
| [Best Practice Auditd Configuration](https://github.com/Neo23x0/auditd) | Florian Roth (Neo23x0) | A commented auditd rule set meant as a baseline for major Linux distributions, with notes on its coverage, validation, sources, and related projects. | Dataset or feed | Free |
| [OpenSCAP](https://www.open-scap.org/) | Red Hat | Tools for scanning a system against a chosen security policy and evaluating its compliance with standards. | Tool | Free |
